data.name: NCMAP001_Title
data.value: Source field not found

data.name: NCMAP001_Message
data.value: The source field '{1}' specified by mapped property '{0}' does not exist in type '{2}'

data.name: NCMAP001_Description
data.value: The DTO property is annotated with [MapProperty] but the specified source field does not exist in the source type; the property will not be mapped.

data.name: NCMAP002_Title
data.value: Type incompatible

data.name: NCMAP002_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' of type '{1}' is incompatible with source field '{2}' of type '{3}'; cannot assign directly or convert implicitly. Fix guidance: check whether the FromField source field type of [MapProperty] matches the target property type, or use [Convert] for a custom conversion.

data.name: NCMAP002_Description
data.value: The target property type is incompatible with the source field type; the runtime TypeConvertHelper fallback will be used, which may produce unexpected behavior.

data.name: NCMAP003_Title
data.value: No mappable properties

data.name: NCMAP003_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' is annotated with [MapFrom(typeof({1}))] but no property can be mapped

data.name: NCMAP003_Description
data.value: The DTO is annotated with [MapFrom] but no property matches the source type; the source type may be specified incorrectly.

data.name: NCMAP005_Title
data.value: Compose cross-table field not found

data.name: NCMAP005_Message
data.value: The field '{2}' specified by [MapProperty(typeof({1}), "{2}")] on property '{0}' does not exist in type '{1}'; the property will not be mapped by Compose

data.name: NCMAP005_Description
data.value: The DTO property is annotated with [MapProperty] specifying a cross-table source field, but the field does not exist in the specified sub-source type; the property will not be mapped during Compose. Check whether the FromSource type and FromField name of [MapProperty] are correct.

data.name: NCMAP006_Title
data.value: Target property unmapped

data.name: NCMAP006_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' (type '{1}') has a same-named property in source type '{2}', but the target setter is {3}; the property will not be mapped. Annotate [MapIgnore] if you intend to ignore it.

data.name: NCMAP006_Description
data.value: The source type has a same-named property, but the target setter is not public (private/protected/internal/init or no setter); generated code cannot assign. Change it to public set, or annotate [MapIgnore] to ignore it explicitly.

data.name: NCMAP007_Title
data.value: Source property unmapped

data.name: NCMAP007_Message
data.value: Property '{1}' (type '{2}') of source type '{0}' has no corresponding target property; this source property will not be mapped

data.name: NCMAP007_Description
data.value: The source property has no corresponding target property; data will not be mapped to the target object. If this is intentional, annotate [MapIgnore] on the source property to silence this hint.

data.name: NCMAP009_Title
data.value: Duplicate mapping of source property

data.name: NCMAP009_Message
data.value: Properties '{0}' and '{1}' both map to the same property '{3}' of source type '{2}'; this may cause duplicate data overwriting

data.name: NCMAP009_Description
data.value: Multiple target properties' [MapProperty] point to the same source property, usually a copy-paste error. Check whether the source field configuration of [MapProperty] is correct.

data.name: NCMAP010_Title
data.value: No overlapping enum members

data.name: NCMAP010_Message
data.value: Source enum '{0}' and target enum '{1}' have no overlapping member names; casting by value may produce unexpected results

data.name: NCMAP010_Description
data.value: For enum-to-enum mapping, the source and target enums have completely different member names. Casting by underlying value may produce unexpected enum values. Check the enum definitions or use [Convert] for a custom conversion.

data.name: NCMAP011_Title
data.value: Non-public type skipped by source generator

data.name: NCMAP011_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' has accessibility '{1}'; the source generator only supports public types. This type will use the runtime engine path and no compile-time code will be generated.

data.name: NCMAP011_Description
data.value: The mapper class generated by the source generator is internal. The current version does not generate compile-time code for non-public types; it automatically falls back to the runtime expression tree engine. Functionality is unaffected, but the AOT-friendliness and zero-reflection benefits of the source generator are not available.

data.name: NCMAP012_Title
data.value: Record circular reference or unresolvable graph; DeepCopy falls back to runtime

data.name: NCMAP012_Message
data.value: The DeepCopy property graph of record type '{0}' contains a circular reference or statically unresolvable edge; it cannot be generated safely via the constructor path and has been fallen back to the runtime path

data.name: NCMAP012_Description
data.value: DeepCopy of record types is generated recursively via constructor arguments, but dst is created inside new T(...), so it cannot be registered in the cycle detection cache before construction. When the property graph contains a circular reference (e.g. record Node(Node? Next)) or statically unresolvable edges (object/interface-typed properties, overridable virtual reference properties), the constructor path cannot defend against cycles and risks infinite recursion. This type automatically falls back to the Mapper.DeepCopyRuntimeOnly runtime path; functionality is unaffected but the performance benefits of the source generator are not available.

data.name: NCMAP016_Title
data.value: DeepCopy graph statically unresolvable; full cycle detection retained

data.name: NCMAP016_Message
data.value: Property '{1}' (type {2}) of type '{0}' cannot be statically resolved for cycle reachability; DeepCopy of this type retains full cycle detection

data.name: NCMAP016_Description
data.value: The deep copy property graph of the type contains statically unresolvable edges (object/dynamic/interface-typed properties, open or unconstrained generic parameters, virtual reference properties overridable by derived classes, etc.). Static analysis cannot prove acyclicity, so DeepCopy of this type retains full cycle detection (CycleCache). Functionality is unaffected, but the zero-detection fast path for acyclic graphs is not available.

data.name: NCMAP013_Title
data.value: Reverse mapping property skipped

data.name: NCMAP013_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' was skipped in reverse mapping ({1} →{2}): {3}

data.name: NCMAP013_Description
data.value: A property from the forward mapping was skipped in reverse mapping. Common reasons: Convert has no source property, the target setter is not public, collection index path reverse registration, or the intermediate node setter of the reverse write-back path is unavailable. This is an inherent semantic limitation, not a configuration error.

data.name: NCMAP031_Title
data.value: Intermediate node of reverse write-back path not instantiable

data.name: NCMAP031_Message
data.value: Intermediate node '{1}' (type {0}) of reverse write-back path '{2}' is not instantiable (interface/abstract class/no public parameterless constructor); reverse mapping ({3} →{4}) cannot create this node; the property is skipped

data.name: NCMAP031_Description
data.value: Reverse path write-back (DTO flat property →entity nested path assignment) must create a new instance when an intermediate node is null. When the intermediate node is an interface, abstract class, or has no public parameterless constructor, it cannot be instantiated; this configuration necessarily fails in the reverse direction (the forward read path is fully legal). Blocked at compile time by an Error diagnostic to avoid generating invalid code (task book B10).

data.name: NCMAP032_Title
data.value: init-only property skipped on update path

data.name: NCMAP032_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is init-only; update mapping ({1} →{2}) cannot assign on an existing target object; the property is skipped (only the creation path can write it)

data.name: NCMAP032_Description
data.value: init-only properties can only be assigned at object construction (the creation path); the update path (an existing target object) cannot assign again, so the generator skips the property. This is a semantic limitation of C# init accessors, not a configuration error.

data.name: NCMAP033_Title
data.value: Reverse mapping does not consume [Convert] by default

data.name: NCMAP033_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with [Convert]; reverse mapping ({1} → {2}) does not consume it by default (the converter's generic binding is the forward direction); the reverse direction writes via the type conversion path. Annotate [ConvertBack] if a custom reverse conversion is needed.

data.name: NCMAP033_Description
data.value: The generic arguments of a [Convert] converter bind the forward direction (entity source type →DTO output type); reverse mapping does not consume the converter by default, and the generator writes via the type conversion path. If a custom reverse conversion is needed, annotate [ConvertBack].

data.name: NCMAP034_Title
data.value: [Mask] property participates in reverse write-back (masked value written back as-is)

data.name: NCMAP034_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with [Mask] and participates in reverse write-back ({1} →{2}); the masked value will be written to the target entity as-is (masking is lossy and irreversible; confirm the business semantics)

data.name: NCMAP034_Description
data.value: [Mask] masking is a lossy (irreversible) operation; reverse write-back writes the masked value back to the entity property as-is, potentially overwriting complete data in the entity. For CRUD update scenarios, annotating [MapIgnore(ToEntity)] on the masked DTO property to block the reverse write-back is recommended.

data.name: NCMAP035_Title
data.value: Converter method not found or inaccessible

data.name: NCMAP035_Message
data.value: Property '{0}': no accessible static method '{1}' on anchor type '{2}'. The method must be declared on the anchor type itself (inherited static methods are not considered), be static, and be public, internal (same assembly), or protected internal (same assembly). For the single-name form the anchor type is the type containing the annotated property; to target a method on another type, use the two-argument form [Convert(typeof(X), nameof(X.M))].

data.name: NCMAP035_Description
data.value: The method-reference form of [Convert]/[ConvertBack] resolves a static method on the anchor type with DeclaredOnly semantics (base-type inheritance is not considered) and the accessibility whitelist public / internal (same assembly) / protected internal (same assembly); private, protected, and private protected methods are rejected. A name that only exists on another type — e.g. the single-name form with nameof(OtherType.M), whose qualifier the compiler silently drops — is reported here; use the two-argument form to target another type.

data.name: NCMAP036_Title
data.value: Converter method overload is ambiguous

data.name: NCMAP036_Message
data.value: Property '{0}': multiple overloads of static method '{1}' on anchor type '{2}' match the signature templates. Rename the method or remove the conflicting overloads; a constructor form that selects an overload by signature is intentionally not provided.

data.name: NCMAP036_Description
data.value: When multiple same-name static overloads on the anchor type pass shape exclusion and signature template matching, the call target is ambiguous. Disambiguate by renaming the method or moving it; overload selection by signature is deliberately not supported.

data.name: NCMAP037_Title
data.value: Converter method signature mismatch

data.name: NCMAP037_Message
data.value: Property '{0}': no overload of static method '{1}' on anchor type '{2}' matches the signature templates (expected return type '{3}'). Details: {4}.

data.name: NCMAP037_Description
data.value: A matching overload must be a non-generic static method without optional/params/ref-out-in parameters, returning the target property type (only non-nullable to nullable lifting is allowed), with parameters exactly equal (after Nullable unwrap; no assignable widening) to T0 M(), T1 M(TField), T2 M(TSource), or T3 M(TSource, TField). Generic anchor types are unsupported in the single-name form; use the two-argument form with a closed generic type.

data.name: NCMAP038_Title
data.value: Lifecycle hook method unresolved

data.name: NCMAP038_Message
data.value: Attribute '{0}': no accessible static method '{1}' was found on anchor type '{2}'. The hook method must be public or internal (same assembly); if the method is declared on a host type other than the annotated DTO, use the two-argument constructor form to specify the host type.

data.name: NCMAP038_Description
data.value: A lifecycle hook attribute ([BeforeMapping]/[AfterMapping]) resolves a static method with the void(TSource, TTarget) signature. The method must be declared on the annotated type (single-argument form) or on the host type passed explicitly (two-argument form), and must be visible to the anchor type as public or same-assembly internal.

data.name: NCMAP039_Title
data.value: Lifecycle hook signature mismatch

data.name: NCMAP039_Message
data.value: Attribute '{0}': method '{1}' does not satisfy the lifecycle hook contract: {2}

data.name: NCMAP039_Description
data.value: A lifecycle hook method must be a static method with the void(TSource, TTarget) signature, with parameter types assignable from the mapping pair. In the single-argument form the anchor type must be a closed (non-open-generic) type; open generic hosts require the two-argument constructor form with a closed generic type.

data.name: NCMAP040_Title
data.value: Lifecycle hook ambiguous overload

data.name: NCMAP040_Message
data.value: Attribute '{0}': multiple accessible overloads of static method '{1}' on anchor type '{2}' are signature-compatible with the mapping pair and none is an exact match; specify a single unambiguous method

data.name: NCMAP040_Description
data.value: When several overloads of a lifecycle hook method are signature-compatible with the mapping pair, an exact match (parameter types equal to the mapping pair types) is required for deterministic resolution.

data.name: NCMAP099_Title
data.value: Source generation failed for mapping

data.name: NCMAP099_Message
data.value: Failed to generate mapping code for {0} →{1}: {2}

data.name: NCMAP099_Description
data.value: An unexpected exception occurred while generating mapping code for a specific type pair. Other mappings are unaffected.

data.name: NCMAP014_Title
data.value: Mask type mismatch

data.name: NCMAP014_Message
data.value: The type specified by [Mask(typeof({1}))] on property '{0}' does not implement the NCMapper.IMask interface

data.name: NCMAP014_Description
data.value: The type specified by [Mask] must implement the NCMapper.IMask interface (string Mask(string? value)).

data.name: NCMAP015_Title
data.value: Mask target property type invalid

data.name: NCMAP015_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with [Mask], but the target property type is '{1}'; masking only supports string-typed properties

data.name: NCMAP015_Description
data.value: [Mask] can only be annotated on string-typed properties (IMask.Mask(string?) →string).

data.name: NCMAP017_Title
data.value: [MapNoAutoInclude] on a reference property

data.name: NCMAP017_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with [MapNoAutoInclude], but it is a reference type (non-collection); automatic Include has significant overhead only for collection navigations, so this annotation is usually meaningless

data.name: NCMAP017_Description
data.value: [MapNoAutoInclude] is designed to exclude the auto-loading overhead of large collection navigations; annotating it on a reference property usually has no practical effect.

data.name: NCMAP018_Title
data.value: Array Contains in expression tree binds to MemoryExtensions.Contains

data.name: NCMAP018_Message
data.value: In an expression tree lambda, Contains on the '{0}' array binds to MemoryExtensions.Contains(ReadOnlySpan<T>, T) under .NET 10/C# 14; ORM expression parsers such as FreeSql only recognize Enumerable.Contains and will throw NotSupportedException. Use {0}.AsEnumerable().Contains(...) or a List<T> instead.

data.name: NCMAP018_Description
data.value: .NET 10/C# 14 overload resolution change: T[].Contains in an expression tree lambda now binds to MemoryExtensions.Contains; FreeSql's expression parser only recognizes Enumerable.Contains and will throw NotSupportedException.

data.name: NCMAP019_Title
data.value: Mapping configuration attributes present without [MapFrom]; the configuration has no activation path

data.name: NCMAP019_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' has mapping configuration attributes ([MapProperty]/[Convert]/[ConvertBack]/[MapIgnore]/[BeforeMapping]/[AfterMapping]/[Mask]/[MapWhen]/[MapNoAutoInclude]/[MapFormat]/[MapNoAutoMatch]) but is not annotated with [MapFrom]; the configuration has no activation path and is silently inert. Annotate [MapFrom] on the configuration-owning side, or remove the attributes (undeclared pairs still map by property name).

data.name: NCMAP019_Description
data.value: Mapping configuration annotations (eleven attribute-level items) are only effective when the containing type has a mapping declaration anchor ([MapFrom] or a Fluent For<S,T>() declaration). An unanchored configuration has no activation path and is silently ignored at runtime. This is a paired-rule compile-time enforcement (Error).

data.name: NCMAP020_Title
data.value: Invalid global mapping configuration value; treated as unset

data.name: NCMAP020_Message
data.value: The value '{1}' of global mapping configuration item '{0}' is invalid ({2}); the item is treated as unset (inheriting lower-level configuration)

data.name: NCMAP020_Description
data.value: When a global mapping configuration value is invalid (enum out of range, unresolvable type full name, list exceeding 8 entries, or complex syntax beyond the MVP scope), the item is treated as unset without blocking compilation, aligned with Mapperly RMG095 behavior.

data.name: NCMAP021_Title
data.value: Explicit annotation hit global ignore (fail-closed ignore)

data.name: NCMAP021_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with an explicit mapping attribute but hits the global ignore list ({1}); the property is ignored. Action: add OverrideIgnore = true to exempt, or remove the redundant annotation (global ignore already covers it).

data.name: NCMAP021_Description
data.value: An explicit annotation ([MapProperty]/[Convert]/[Mask]/[ConvertBack]) hits the global ignore without OverrideIgnore, so it is ignored fail-closed; the message gives two-way guidance (exempt via OverrideIgnore, or remove the redundant annotation).

data.name: NCMAP022_Title
data.value: [MapIgnore] and OverrideIgnore=true are contradictory

data.name: NCMAP022_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with both [MapIgnore] and OverrideIgnore=true, a contradictory configuration: the ignore takes effect ([MapIgnore] does not participate in the global ignore exemption). Remove either [MapIgnore] or OverrideIgnore=true.

data.name: NCMAP022_Description
data.value: The property-level [MapIgnore] is an explicit ignore and does not participate in the OverrideIgnore exemption; annotating both with OverrideIgnore=true is contradictory, and the ignore takes effect (fail-closed semantics).

data.name: NCMAP023_Title
data.value: Enum member names differ only by case; string→enum degrades to exact match

data.name: NCMAP023_Message
data.value: Enum type '{0}' has member names that differ only by case (violates the CLS specification); string→enum conversion degrades to exact name matching (case-sensitive). Rename the members to remove the ambiguity.

data.name: NCMAP023_Description
data.value: When enum member names collide except for case (e.g. Red and RED), the string→enum generated switch degrades to exact matching (case-sensitive); invalid values still throw MapException. Such enums violate the CLS specification; renaming the members is recommended.

data.name: NCMAP024_Title
data.value: Duplicate enum member values; string→enum numeric labels degraded

data.name: NCMAP024_Message
data.value: Enum type '{0}' has members with duplicate values (alias enum); the numeric-string label dimension of string→enum degrades to exact name matching, so numeric strings (e.g. "1") cannot be converted on the generated side. Eliminate the duplicate values or use [Convert].

data.name: NCMAP024_Description
data.value: When enum member values are duplicated (alias enum), numeric-string labels would produce duplicate switch labels; the numeric-string dimension degrades to exact name matching and this diagnostic is emitted.

data.name: NCMAP025_Title
data.value: Mutual mapping declaration (double true)

data.name: NCMAP025_Message
data.value: Types '{0}' and '{1}' declare the mapping relationship on both sides ([MapFrom] or Fluent For), forming a mutual declaration. Remove one side's declaration; the pair is not generated and the runtime falls back to name matching.

data.name: NCMAP025_Description
data.value: For a double-true mutual reference (A [MapFrom(B)] and B [MapFrom(A)]), the generated side cannot define a unique generation source; the pair is not generated and an Error-level diagnostic is emitted (build fails). The runtime falls back to name matching; removing one declaration restores generation.

data.name: NCMAP026_Title
data.value: Mask annotation in non-canonical position (source side)

data.name: NCMAP026_Message
data.value: Non-canonical annotation position — [Mask] should be annotated on the target side (same side as [MapFrom]); source-side annotation has no effect. Move [Mask] to the target property.

data.name: NCMAP026_Description
data.value: When the class carrying the Mask annotation differs from the class annotated with [MapFrom] (Mask on the source side), the source-side Mask annotation has no effect (Mask semantics are one-way: masking the target string); a Warning is emitted suggesting the canonical position. For mutual reference pairs, NCMAP025 takes precedence and this diagnostic is not stacked.

data.name: NCMAP027_Title
data.value: Incompatible member skipped (AutoMapper semantics aligned)

data.name: NCMAP027_Message
data.value: Mapping property '{0}' skipped: source type '{1}' and target type '{2}' are incompatible (aligned with AutoMapper semantics; this member is not mapped)

data.name: NCMAP027_Description
data.value: When auto-matched same-named properties under [MapFrom] have completely incompatible source/target types, mapping is skipped (aligned with AutoMapper's semantics of not mapping incompatible members) and an Info hint is emitted; an explicit [MapProperty(FromField=...)] incompatibility still goes through the NCMAP002 fallback.

data.name: NCMAP028_Title
data.value: Inaccessible member skipped

data.name: NCMAP028_Message
data.value: Mapping property '{0}' skipped: member '{1}' is inaccessible (visibility {2}; generated code only accesses public)

data.name: NCMAP028_Description
data.value: Generated code can only access public members (cross-assembly access to internal/protected/private triggers CS0122); inaccessible members are skipped and an Info hint is emitted.

data.name: NCMAP029_Title
data.value: Nested mutual-call cycle degraded

data.name: NCMAP029_Message
data.value: Nested mutual-call cycle detected: '{0}' →'{1}' call each other via nested property delegates —registration pairs on the cycle are degraded and skipped (target properties keep their default values, preventing StackOverflow)

data.name: NCMAP029_Description
data.value: The DTOs of two registration pairs reference each other's DTOs via nested properties (mutual calls in generated code without depth counting); registration pairs on the cycle are degraded and skipped to prevent StackOverflow from cyclic data. Direct self-reference is kept safe by depth protection.

data.name: NCMAP030_Title
data.value: Dot path does not consume [Mask]/[Convert]

data.name: NCMAP030_Message
data.value: The explicit dot path '{1}' of property '{0}' does not consume [{2}] (mapped values are not masked/converted); consumption fix is scheduled for phase B

data.name: NCMAP030_Description
data.value: The explicit dot path mapping succeeds, but the generated side does not consume [Mask]/[Convert]: the target property is not masked/converted. This is a known limitation of the current version (consumption added in phase B); this diagnostic only guarantees observability and does not block mapping.

data.name: NCMAP_F02_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda property not found

data.name: NCMAP_F02_Message
data.value: The property '{0}' referenced by the Fluent lambda does not exist on type '{1}'

data.name: NCMAP_F02_Description
data.value: A lambda in the Fluent chain references a property that cannot be resolved on the declared source/target type (typo or insufficient accessibility). The declaration is skipped; fix the property name or make the property accessible.

data.name: NCMAP_F04_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda root is not a parameter

data.name: NCMAP_F04_Message
data.value: Fluent lambdas cannot reference local variables or static classes; only property paths starting from the lambda parameter are supported

data.name: NCMAP_F04_Description
data.value: The root expression of the lambda is not the lambda parameter (e.g. a local variable or a static class reference). The Fluent channel only supports pure property paths rooted at the lambda parameter; the declaration is skipped.

data.name: NCMAP_F05_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda null-conditional access

data.name: NCMAP_F05_Message
data.value: Fluent lambdas do not support null-conditional access '{0}'; use a direct property path instead

data.name: NCMAP_F05_Description
data.value: The lambda body contains a null-conditional access '?.' which cannot be statically resolved into a property path. Replace it with a direct property path; the declaration is skipped.

data.name: NCMAP_F06_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda indexer access

data.name: NCMAP_F06_Message
data.value: Fluent lambdas do not support indexer access '{0}'

data.name: NCMAP_F06_Description
data.value: The lambda body contains an indexer access '[]' which cannot be statically resolved into a property path. The declaration is skipped; use a direct property path instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F07_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda method call

data.name: NCMAP_F07_Message
data.value: Fluent lambdas do not support method calls '{0}'; only property paths are supported

data.name: NCMAP_F07_Description
data.value: The lambda body contains a method invocation '()' which cannot be statically resolved into a property path. The declaration is skipped; extract the computed value via an explicit static converter if needed.

data.name: NCMAP_F08_Title
data.value: Fluent dynamic configuration rejected

data.name: NCMAP_F08_Message
data.value: Dynamic configuration statement '{0}' is not allowed in the Fluent Configure method body; only pure chained static calls are supported

data.name: NCMAP_F08_Description
data.value: The Configure method body contains control flow (if/for/foreach/while/switch/try), a ternary expression, an assignment, or a local variable declaration. The Fluent channel only supports statically analyzable pure chains; the offending statement is rejected.

data.name: NCMAP_F11_Title
data.value: Dual-driver type pair conflict

data.name: NCMAP_F11_Message
data.value: [MapFrom] on DTO class '{0}' and Fluent Configure on mapper class '{1}' both declare the type pair ({2}, {3}), violating the mutual-exclusion rule; remove one of the declarations

data.name: NCMAP_F11_Description
data.value: The same (Source, Target) type pair is declared by both the [MapFrom] attribute channel and the Fluent Configure channel. Both channels write the same GeneratedCache slot and would produce duplicate generated methods; both declarations are suppressed. Using the two channels for different type pairs (pattern coexistence) is allowed.

data.name: NCMAP_F12_Title
data.value: AfterMapping target method is private

data.name: NCMAP_F12_Message
data.value: The AfterMapping target method '{0}' is private and inaccessible across classes; generated code lives in the GeneratedMapper static class (a separate type), so the target method must be public or internal static

data.name: NCMAP_F12_Description
data.value: The AfterMapping target method's accessibility makes it unreachable from the generated GeneratedMapper static class. Promote the method to public or internal static so the generated invocation compiles.

data.name: NCMAP_F14_Title
data.value: AfterMapping target is not a method group

data.name: NCMAP_F14_Message
data.value: The AfterMapping target must be a statically resolvable method group reference; lambdas/closures/captured variables cannot be statically resolved as generated-code references

data.name: NCMAP_F14_Description
data.value: AfterMapping requires a method group reference that the source generator can emit as a direct call in generated code. Lambdas, closures, captured variables, and local functions have no statically addressable entry point; the declaration is skipped.

data.name: NCMAP_F15_Title
data.value: MapperConfig class has no matching method

data.name: NCMAP_F15_Message
data.value: The [MapperConfig] class '{0}' contains no method matching the required signature; the Fluent channel entry convention is 'public static void M(NCMapper.FluentMappingConfig cfg)' with any method name

data.name: NCMAP_F15_Description
data.value: The class is annotated with [MapperConfig] (explicit Fluent channel intent) but declares no 'static void M(NCMapper.FluentMappingConfig cfg)' method. Add such a method to declare mappings, or remove the attribute.

data.name: NCMAP_F16_Title
data.value: Fluent type pair duplicate declaration

data.name: NCMAP_F16_Message
data.value: The type pair ({0}, {1}) is declared {2} times in the Fluent channel (mapper classes: {3}); all duplicate declarations are suppressed and no mapping method is generated; merge them into a single declaration or remove the duplicates

data.name: NCMAP_F16_Description
data.value: Declaring the same (Source, Target) type pair more than once in the Fluent channel (across [MapperConfig] classes or via multiple chains in one Configure) would generate duplicate methods with the same name and fail at the consumer side with CS0111. Every conflicting declaration is suppressed and each declaration site reports this error. Merge the declarations into a single chain or remove the duplicates.

data.name: NCMAP_F17_Title
data.value: Fluent declaration conflict: Ignore + ConvertBack

data.name: NCMAP_F17_Message
data.value: Fluent declaration conflict: property '{0}' on '{1}' declares both Ignore and ConvertBack — reverse write would never execute

data.name: NCMAP_F17_Description
data.value: The same DTO anchor property is declared with both Ignore and ConvertBack in one chain. Ignore removes the property from mapping candidates (no forward property mapping means no reverse derivation), so the ConvertBack reverse write would never execute. Remove the Ignore declaration or the ConvertBack declaration.

data.name: NCMAP_F18_Title
data.value: ConvertBack reverse target not found

data.name: NCMAP_F18_Message
data.value: ConvertBack reverse target not found: no property '{0}' on source type '{1}' (anchor '{2}' on '{3}')

data.name: NCMAP_F18_Description
data.value: The ConvertBack anchor property name has no same-name property (case-insensitive) on the source (entity) type, so the reverse write has no target. Add the property to the entity type, rename the anchor, or remove the ConvertBack declaration.

data.name: NCMAP_F19_Title
data.value: ConvertBack converter not accessible from generated code

data.name: NCMAP_F19_Message
data.value: ConvertBack converter '{0}' must be public/internal static and accessible from generated code (same assembly)

data.name: NCMAP_F19_Description
data.value: The ConvertBack converter method is declared private or protected. Generated code lives in an internal static class within the same assembly and cannot access such members; generated calls would fail with CS0122. Make the converter public or internal static, or move it into a class visible to the generated code.

data.name: NCMAP_F20_Title
data.value: ConvertBack converter must be a static method group or a transcribable lambda

data.name: NCMAP_F20_Message
data.value: ConvertBack converter must be a statically resolvable method group, or a capture-free expression lambda (transcribed into generated code); closures/local functions/instance bindings remain unsupported

data.name: NCMAP_F20_Description
data.value: The ConvertBack converter argument resolved to a delegate variable or an instance method bound to a receiver, which has no statically addressable entry point. Pass a public/internal static method group, or an inline capture-free expression lambda (transcribed into a private static method of the generated mapper). Lambdas that capture variables, access private/protected members, or use statement bodies are rejected with NCMAP_F41/NCMAP_F42.

data.name: NCMAP_F21_Title
data.value: ConvertBack converter signature mismatch

data.name: NCMAP_F21_Message
data.value: ConvertBack converter '{0}' matches no supported shape; expected one of: M() / M(TField) / M(TSource) / M(TSource, TField) with TField='{1}', TSource='{2}', return '{3}'

data.name: NCMAP_F21_Description
data.value: The ConvertBack converter signature matches none of the four supported shapes (T0 constant / T1 field value / T2 whole source / T3 combined, including Nullable guard variants). Generic methods, optional parameters, params arrays, and ref/out/in parameters are also excluded. Align the converter signature with the anchor property type, the DTO type, and the entity-side property type.

data.name: NCMAP_F22_Title
data.value: ConvertBack anchor property has no public setter or init accessor

data.name: NCMAP_F22_Message
data.value: ConvertBack anchor property '{0}' on '{1}' has no public setter or init accessor — the declaration will be ignored by materialization; consider adding a public or init setter, or use the attribute channel with entity-side [ConvertBack]

data.name: NCMAP_F22_Description
data.value: Although a ConvertBack declaration only reads the DTO anchor property, the materialization traversal drops properties without a public setter before declarations are processed (the same write gate that protects forward mapping). The declaration is therefore silently ignored. Add a public or init setter to the anchor property, or express the reverse conversion via the attribute channel with an entity-side [ConvertBack] annotation (the ReverseOnly path does not pass through the DTO traversal gate).

data.name: NCMAP_F23_Title
data.value: Fluent declaration conflict: Ignore + Convert

data.name: NCMAP_F23_Message
data.value: Fluent declaration conflict: property '{0}' on '{1}' declares both Ignore and Convert — forward conversion would never execute

data.name: NCMAP_F23_Description
data.value: The same target property is declared with both Ignore and Convert in one chain. Ignore removes the property from mapping candidates (no property mapping means no converter attachment), so the Convert forward conversion would never execute. Remove the Ignore declaration or the Convert declaration.

data.name: NCMAP_F24_Title
data.value: Convert source property not found

data.name: NCMAP_F24_Message
data.value: Convert source not found: no source property '{0}' on '{1}' for anchor '{2}' (same-name, flattening, and [MapProperty] reverse lookup all failed)

data.name: NCMAP_F24_Description
data.value: The source-side resolution flow (same-name property, automatic flattening, [MapProperty] reverse lookup) found no source property for the Convert anchor, so the declaration has no source input and is dropped. Unlike the attribute channel's converter-with-no-source form (which emits a default(TField) call), the Fluent channel requires a reachable source property. Ensure a same-name source property exists, or one reachable via flattening or a [MapProperty] reverse annotation.

data.name: NCMAP_F25_Title
data.value: Convert converter not accessible from generated code

data.name: NCMAP_F25_Message
data.value: Convert converter '{0}' must be public/internal static and accessible from generated code (same assembly)

data.name: NCMAP_F25_Description
data.value: The Convert converter method is declared private or protected. Generated code lives in an internal static class within the same assembly and cannot access such members; generated calls would fail with CS0122. Make the converter public or internal static, or move it into a class visible to the generated code.

data.name: NCMAP_F26_Title
data.value: Convert converter must be a static method group or a transcribable lambda

data.name: NCMAP_F26_Message
data.value: Convert converter must be a statically resolvable method group, or a capture-free expression lambda (transcribed into generated code); closures/local functions/instance bindings remain unsupported

data.name: NCMAP_F26_Description
data.value: The Convert converter argument resolved to a delegate variable or an instance method bound to a receiver, which has no statically addressable entry point. Pass a public/internal static method group, or an inline capture-free expression lambda (transcribed into a private static method of the generated mapper). Lambdas that capture variables, access private/protected members, or use statement bodies are rejected with NCMAP_F41/NCMAP_F42.

data.name: NCMAP_F27_Title
data.value: Convert converter signature mismatch

data.name: NCMAP_F27_Message
data.value: Convert converter '{0}' matches none of the supported shapes; expected M() / M(TField) / M(TSource) / M(TSource, TField) with TField='{1}', TSource='{2}', returning '{3}'

data.name: NCMAP_F27_Description
data.value: The Convert converter signature matches none of the four supported shapes (T0 constant / T1 field value / T2 whole source / T3 combined, including Nullable guard variants). Generic methods, optional parameters, params arrays, and ref/out/in parameters are also excluded. Align the converter signature with the source property type, the source entity type, and the anchor property type.

data.name: NCMAP_F28_Title
data.value: Convert anchor property has no public setter or init accessor

data.name: NCMAP_F28_Message
data.value: Convert anchor property '{0}' on '{1}' has no public setter or init accessor — the declaration will be ignored by materialization; consider adding a public or init setter, or use the attribute channel with [Convert] on the property

data.name: NCMAP_F28_Description
data.value: Although a Convert declaration only reads the source side, the materialization traversal drops target properties without a public setter before declarations are processed (the same write gate that protects forward mapping). The declaration is therefore silently ignored. Add a public or init setter to the anchor property, or express the conversion via the attribute channel with a [Convert] annotation on the property.

data.name: NCMAP_F29_Title
data.value: Fluent declaration conflict: main chain × FromSource binding / multiple bindings on one sub-source

data.name: NCMAP_F29_Message
data.value: Fluent declaration conflict: property '{0}' on '{1}' — a main-chain declaration and a FromSource sub-source binding cannot target the same property (a property can be fed by only one source); multiple path-carrying bindings (Map/MapTree) or multiple Convert declarations on the same sub-source also conflict (a single Convert/Mask/FromJson is attach-only and not counted)

data.name: NCMAP_F29_Description
data.value: A target property cannot simultaneously participate in the primary-source mapping chain and in a FromSource sub-source binding: the FromSource binding feeds the property from a sub-source, while the main-chain declaration feeds it from the primary source (or excludes/transforms it), which is ambiguous; multiple path-carrying bindings (Map/MapTree) on the same sub-source likewise create multi-source ambiguity (Mask/FromJson are attach-only and not counted; a Convert combined with a Map is merged as an attachment, while multiple Convert declarations on the same sub-source still conflict). Keep exactly one declaration, or bind the property to a different sub-source.

data.name: NCMAP_F30_Title
data.value: ConvertBack is not allowed inside a FromSource block

data.name: NCMAP_F30_Message
data.value: ConvertBack is not supported inside a FromSource block (sub-source '{0}') — the FromSource binding is forward-only and has no reverse write-back target

data.name: NCMAP_F30_Description
data.value: The FromSource sub-source binding only performs forward sub-source to target mapping. Reverse write-back (ConvertBack) has no semantic landing point inside a sub-source block; move the conversion to the main chain or the attribute channel.

data.name: NCMAP_F31_Title
data.value: NoAutoInclude is not allowed inside a FromSource block

data.name: NCMAP_F31_Message
data.value: NoAutoInclude is not supported inside a FromSource block (sub-source '{0}') — sub-source fields are always explicitly declared, so there is no auto-inclusion to disable

data.name: NCMAP_F31_Description
data.value: Inside a FromSource sub-source block every bound field must be declared explicitly; the primary-source auto-include machinery does not apply to sub-source blocks, so NoAutoInclude has no effect there.

data.name: NCMAP_F32_Title
data.value: AfterMapping is not allowed inside a FromSource block

data.name: NCMAP_F32_Message
data.value: AfterMapping is not supported inside a FromSource block (sub-source '{0}') — the generated Compose pipeline has no hook injection point; the hook would never run

data.name: NCMAP_F32_Description
data.value: The runtime Compose pipeline (generated delegate or ComposeRuntime fallback) provides no after-mapping hook injection point, so an AfterMapping declared inside a sub-source block could never execute. Declare the hook on the main chain instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F35_Title
data.value: BeforeMapping target method is private

data.name: NCMAP_F35_Message
data.value: The BeforeMapping target method '{0}' is private and inaccessible across classes; generated code lives in the GeneratedMapper static class (a separate type), so the target method must be public or internal static

data.name: NCMAP_F35_Description
data.value: The BeforeMapping target method's accessibility makes it unreachable from the generated GeneratedMapper static class. Promote the method to public or internal static so the generated invocation compiles.

data.name: NCMAP_F36_Title
data.value: BeforeMapping target is not a method group

data.name: NCMAP_F36_Message
data.value: The BeforeMapping target must be a statically resolvable method group reference; lambdas/closures/captured variables cannot be statically resolved as generated-code references

data.name: NCMAP_F36_Description
data.value: BeforeMapping requires a method group reference that the source generator can emit as a direct call in generated code. Lambdas, closures, captured variables, and local functions have no statically addressable entry point; the declaration is skipped.

data.name: NCMAP_F37_Title
data.value: BeforeMapping target has no insertion point (constructor-integrated form)

data.name: NCMAP_F37_Message
data.value: Target type '{0}' constructs via a parameterized/init-only constructor whose construction and assignment are inseparable, so the BeforeMapping hook cannot be emitted before any assignment; use a settable-property target or remove the hook

data.name: NCMAP_F37_Description
data.value: BeforeMapping must run after the target instance exists but before the first property assignment. Constructor-integrated targets (records with all-init properties, positional records, immutable constructors) have no such point; the generator reports this instead of silently dropping the hook.

data.name: NCMAP_F38_Title
data.value: BeforeMapping is not allowed inside a FromSource block

data.name: NCMAP_F38_Message
data.value: BeforeMapping is not supported inside a FromSource block (sub-source '{0}') — the generated Compose pipeline has no hook injection point; the hook would never run

data.name: NCMAP_F38_Description
data.value: The runtime Compose pipeline (generated delegate or ComposeRuntime fallback) provides no before-mapping hook injection point, so a BeforeMapping declared inside a sub-source block could never execute. Declare the hook on the main chain instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F39_Title
data.value: Same-kind lifecycle hook declared on both channels for one mapping pair

data.name: NCMAP_F39_Message
data.value: Both channels declare the same-kind '{0}' hook for {1} → {2}: attribute side '{3}' vs Fluent side '{4}'; declare the hook on only one channel

data.name: NCMAP_F39_Description
data.value: Before×Before / After×After coexistence on the same (source, target) pair is a semantic error — silently merging the two hook declarations would make the executed one depend on channel arbitration order. Cross combinations (attribute After + Fluent Before) do not conflict. Hook refs are only counted after signature-applicability filtering.

data.name: NCMAP_F40_Title
data.value: MapWhen predicate method contract violated

data.name: NCMAP_F40_Message
data.value: MapWhen predicate '{0}' failed its contract: {1}. The predicate must be a statically addressable public/internal static method group with signature static bool M(T) where the parameter equals the source field type (T1) or the source entity type (T2).

data.name: NCMAP_F40_Description
data.value: The named method-group form of MapWhen requires a public or internal static method visible from generated code. Rejections cover: unresolvable method group (delegate variable / instance binding), non-static methods, signature mismatch (single parameter returning bool, no ref/out/in), insufficient visibility, and missing implicit conversion from the source field type to the predicate parameter type.

data.name: NCMAP_F41_Title
data.value: Inline lambda captures variables or accesses private members

data.name: NCMAP_F41_Message
data.value: Inline expression cannot be transcribed: {0} ('{1}'). Captured outer locals/parameters/local functions/this and private or protected member access cannot be emitted into the generated static method — move the logic into a named static method and use the method-group form instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F41_Description
data.value: The transcription engine emits inline lambdas as private static methods, which have no closure semantics. References to outer-scope state (locals, parameters, local functions, this) or to members inaccessible from generated code (private/protected) are rejected at the exact sub-expression location rather than producing semantically divergent code.

data.name: NCMAP_F42_Title
data.value: Inline lambda contains statement body or non-transcribable nodes

data.name: NCMAP_F42_Message
data.value: Inline expression cannot be transcribed ('{0}'): {1}. Only expression-bodied lambdas over the whitelisted node set (member chains, arithmetic/comparison, conditional access, static and instance calls, nameof, literals) can be transcribed into the generated code.

data.name: NCMAP_F42_Description
data.value: Statement-bodied lambdas, dynamic bindings, unsafe/await/query syntax and other non-whitelisted nodes have no semantics-preserving textual transcription. The diagnostic points at the exact offending sub-expression. Extract the logic into a named static method (method-group form) to express it.

data.name: NCMAP_F43_Title
data.value: MapWhen guard anchor has no mapping

data.name: NCMAP_F43_Message
data.value: MapWhen anchor property '{0}' on {1} has no mapping to guard: the property has no auto-matched source and no explicit .Map declaration, or it is excluded by a static .Ignore declaration — the guard would never take effect

data.name: NCMAP_F43_Description
data.value: A conditional guard must attach to a property that actually gets mapped. Anchoring a guard on an unmapped or statically ignored property is a declaration error (likely a typo or leftover) and is rejected at compile time instead of being silently dropped.

data.name: NCMAP_F44_Title
data.value: Duplicate MapWhen declaration on one property

data.name: NCMAP_F44_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' on {1} declares MapWhen more than once: a mapping carries a single condition — express negative filtering by negating the predicate, or combine multiple criteria inside one predicate

data.name: NCMAP_F44_Description
data.value: MapWhen is single-condition by design. Two guards on the same property would make the effective condition depend on conjunction/disjunction intent that the API cannot express; declare one predicate and compose the criteria inside it.

data.name: NCMAP_F45_Title
data.value: MapWhen declared on a main-chain Compose-only mapping

data.name: NCMAP_F45_Message
data.value: MapWhen anchor property '{0}' on {1} is only covered by a FromSource cross-source mapping: the main-chain Compose generator does not expand per-property assignment chains, so the guard has no emission site. Declare the guard inside the FromSource block instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F45_Description
data.value: Inside a FromSource block the sub-mapping assignments are emitted (Update_{Sub}_To_{Target}), so a block-internal MapWhen has a real emission site. On the main chain, a property covered only by cross-source bindings never enters the per-property assignment generation, and silently dropping a filter is a correctness hazard — the declaration is rejected instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F46_Title
data.value: [MapSubclass] type arguments do not satisfy the inheritance contract

data.name: NCMAP_F46_Message
data.value: [MapSubclass(typeof({0}), typeof({1}))] on {2}: the source type must derive from the base pair source {3} and the target type must derive from the base pair target {4} (the attribute form has no generic constraint, so this check runs at extraction time)

data.name: NCMAP_F46_Description
data.value: Unlike the Fluent terminal MapSubclass<TSrcDerived, TTargetDerived>() whose where clauses reject invalid arguments at the call site (CS0311/CS0314), the attribute form accepts arbitrary typeof arguments. The extractor validates the inheritance relation; a failing registration is dropped (no dispatch entry is produced).

data.name: NCMAP_F47_Title
data.value: Invalid MapSubclass registration (duplicate pair or base-type self registration)

data.name: NCMAP_F47_Message
data.value: MapSubclass registration on ({0}, {1}) is invalid ({2}): "duplicate-pair" = the exact same (TSrcDerived, TTargetDerived) pair registered twice (the first is kept); "base-self" = TSrcDerived equals TSource, dispatching the base pair to itself creates an infinite loop (rejected). Partially overlapping registrations (same source at different levels or same source to different targets) are legal and resolved by most-derived-first arbitration.

data.name: NCMAP_F47_Description
data.value: Two invalid forms share this code: (1) the exact same (TSrcDerived, TTargetDerived) pair registered twice — the dispatch chain only needs one entry; (2) TSrcDerived equals TSource — the generic constraint allows a type to satisfy where TSrcDerived : TSource with itself, but dispatching a base pair to its own method creates an infinite self-referencing loop. Both are rejected at materialization time.

data.name: NCMAP_F48_Title
data.value: MapSubclass registered target has no mappable surface

data.name: NCMAP_F48_Message
data.value: MapSubclass registration ({0}, {1}) on ({2}, {3}) produces no mappable output: the derived target type has no public mappable surface or fails construction constraints (synthesized snapshot is skipped or has zero property mappings)

data.name: NCMAP_F48_Description
data.value: The synthesized subclass pair reuses the regular single-pair generation pipeline; when the derived target exposes no public writable/constructible surface the synthesized snapshot is skipped. The registration is reported as empty (fail-fast) instead of silently dropping subclass-specific fields.

data.name: NCMAP_F49_Title
data.value: [MapSubclass] annotation lacks a [MapFrom] anchor

data.name: NCMAP_F49_Message
data.value: [MapSubclass(typeof({0}), typeof({1}))] on {2}: the annotated class has no [MapFrom] anchor, so no base mapping pair exists to consume the registration — the subclass pair is never referenced by any dispatch surface

data.name: NCMAP_F49_Description
data.value: Attribute-side polymorphic registration anchors on the base DTO class that carries [MapFrom] (the declaration carrier of the attribute channel). An orphan [MapSubclass] without that anchor has no base pair; annotate the base DTO with [MapFrom(typeof(BaseSource))] or move the registration to a Fluent .For<TSource, TTarget>().MapSubclass(...) chain.

data.name: NCMAP_F50_Title
data.value: Polymorphic dispatch advisory (reverse asymmetry / dual-instance fallback surface)

data.name: NCMAP_F50_Message
data.value: ({0}, {1}) has MapSubclass registrations; advisories: {2} — "reverse-asymmetry" = the reverse base pair is generated but never dispatches (O-2: the reverse destination is a caller-supplied entity, subclass-specific fields are not populated); "dual-instance-fallback" = Update/MapListInto use dual-instance matching, when the destination's runtime type is not the registered subclass target the base-class body runs and subclass-specific fields are not written. Both are by-design semantics; this Info makes the silent surfaces visible.

data.name: NCMAP_F50_Description
data.value: Static, compile-time advisory (emitted once per pair when SubclassPairs is non-empty): (2) the reverse base pair does not dispatch — reverse mapping targets a caller-supplied entity instance (dst is fixed), so reverse subclass fields are never populated; (3) Update/MapListInto use dual-instance matching — when the destination's runtime type is not the registered subclass target, the base-class body runs and subclass-specific fields are not written. Both are by-design semantics (O-2 ruling); this Info makes the silent surfaces visible.

data.name: NCMAP_F51_Title
data.value: MapCtorParam binding source property not found

data.name: NCMAP_F51_Message
data.value: .MapCtorParam("{0}", "{1}") on {2}: the source property '{1}' does not exist on the source type or has no readable getter — pass a single-segment lambda (form 1) or a valid public property name (form 2)

data.name: NCMAP_F51_Description
data.value: The string form of the explicit constructor-parameter binding resolves the source property by name at extraction time (single-point resolution). A misspelled or non-readable name would otherwise silently bind nothing and the constructor parameter would fall back to default/null without any diagnostic.

data.name: NCMAP_F52_Title
data.value: MapCtorParam target constructor parameter not found

data.name: NCMAP_F52_Message
data.value: .MapCtorParam("{0}", ...) on {1}: no public constructor of the target type declares a bindable parameter named '{0}' (by-ref/pointer parameters cannot be bound). Available parameter names: {2}.

data.name: NCMAP_F52_Description
data.value: The binding parameter name must exist in the parameter set of at least one public constructor of the target type. When it exists in only some candidates, that constructor is preferred by the selector weighting; by-ref/pointer parameters are excluded from the comparison. The message lists the available parameter names to fix the typo.

data.name: NCMAP_F53_Title
data.value: MapCtorParam duplicate binding / conflict with .Map on the same constructor parameter

data.name: NCMAP_F53_Message
data.value: .MapCtorParam("{0}", ...) on {1}: {2}. Duplicate bindings on the same constructor parameter or a binding that targets a parameter also fed by an explicit .Map entry are contradictory declarations (fail-fast, not a silent override).

data.name: NCMAP_F53_Description
data.value: Two MapCtorParam calls naming the same constructor parameter (duplicate) or a MapCtorParam whose parameter name matches an explicit .Map declaration target (map-conflict, record same-name scenario) are contradictory — aligned with the F39 dual-declaration / NCMAP_F23 same-anchor conflict discipline. Remove one of the declarations; for record name-mismatch pairs the existing .Map already solves the binding.

data.name: NCMAP_F54_Title
data.value: Ambiguous equal-parameter-count constructors (advisory)

data.name: NCMAP_F54_Message
data.value: {0}: {1} public constructors tie on the maximum parameter count — the generated selector silently picks by parameter count. Declare .MapCtorParam to make the constructor choice explicit and disambiguate.

data.name: NCMAP_F54_Description
data.value: Mechanical criterion: more than one public constructor ties on the maximum parameter count AND the MapCtorParam binding set is empty. With bindings present the selector weighting already resolves the choice, so no advisory is emitted. Run-time constructor resolution keeps its current silent behavior (declared blind spot).

data.name: NCMAP_F55_Title
data.value: Fluent multi-segment destination path

data.name: NCMAP_F55_Message
data.value: Fluent destinations support a single property only; '{0}' is a multi-segment path

data.name: NCMAP_F55_Description
data.value: The destination lambda resolves to more than one path segment (for example d.Address.City). A Fluent declaration maps exactly one target property, so the declaration is skipped. Use a single property path instead, or declare the nested mapping separately.

data.name: NCMAP_F56_Title
data.value: Fluent property argument is not a lambda expression

data.name: NCMAP_F56_Message
data.value: Fluent property arguments must be lambda expressions; '{0}' is not

data.name: NCMAP_F56_Description
data.value: A destination or source argument does not resolve to a lambda expression (method group, delegate variable, or other expression), so the property path cannot be determined and no mapping is generated for this declaration. Pass an inline lambda such as d => d.Name.

data.name: NCMAP_F57_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda block body or conditional expression

data.name: NCMAP_F57_Message
data.value: Fluent property paths do not support block bodies or conditional expressions ('{0}')

data.name: NCMAP_F57_Description
data.value: The lambda body is a statement block or contains a conditional (?:) expression that cannot be reduced to a property path, so the declaration is skipped. Use a plain expression-bodied property path; conditional logic belongs to a [MapWhen] guard or a converter.

data.name: NCMAP_F58_Title
data.value: Fluent argument is not statically evaluable

data.name: NCMAP_F58_Message
data.value: Fluent argument '{0}' is not statically evaluable; the value is ignored and the default applies

data.name: NCMAP_F58_Description
data.value: The overrideIgnore/Direction argument must be a literal, an enum member, or a const identifier so the source generator can evaluate it at compile time. The declaration is still generated, but the argument value is ignored and the default applies (overrideIgnore=false, direction=Both). Use a semantic constant argument instead.

data.name: NCMAP_F59_Title
data.value: True conflict between Fluent declarations on the same member

data.name: NCMAP_F59_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' has a true conflict: the {1} declaration conflicts with the {2} declaration (same-slot repetition, or coexistence with an ignore). True conflicts are rejected — keep only one declaration or resolve the conflict; see the conflict list for legal combinations.

data.name: NCMAP_F59_Description
data.value: Only true conflicts are reported (error level): ignore vs. any mapping operation, mask/format vs. tree recursion, mask vs. JSON expansion, format vs. JSON expansion, and same-dimension repetition (same slot or same kind across member segments). Conflict-free scenarios (single source with single transform, or newly opened combinations such as explicit source + mask/format) produce no diagnostic.

data.name: NCMAP_F60_Title
data.value: Unknown Fluent chain terminal drops declarations

data.name: NCMAP_F60_Message
data.value: Fluent chain method '{0}' is not a recognized terminal; its declaration is skipped (in a main chain the entire chain is dropped). Remove the unrecognized call or use a supported terminal.

data.name: NCMAP_F60_Description
data.value: The chain parser dispatches on method names extracted from syntax. Object-inherited members (e.g. ToString) or unrelated extension methods compile fine but are not Fluent terminals; in a main chain such a node causes the whole chain snapshot to be dropped without further diagnostics, while a block statement skips only that node. The drop semantics are unchanged — this diagnostic makes the loss visible.

data.name: NCMAP_F62_Title
data.value: Fluent lambda source chain exceeds the maximum member access depth

data.name: NCMAP_F62_Message
data.value: The source chain of the Fluent lambda exceeds the maximum member access depth of {0}; the declaration is dropped. Split the chain into intermediate projections or flatten the source hierarchy.

data.name: NCMAP_F62_Description
data.value: The lambda parser walks member access segments recursively without a bound; an unbounded deep chain can exhaust parser depth and silently snapshot ultra-deep paths. Chains within the configured depth limit remain legal; deeper chains are rejected with this warning.

data.name: NCMAP_F63_Title
data.value: Cycle detection stopped: registered-mapping graph exceeds the visit budget

data.name: NCMAP_F63_Message
data.value: Cycle detection for mapping pair '{0}' stopped after exceeding the visit budget of {1}; the result for this start point is undetermined (no NCMAP029 is emitted and no degradation is marked). Consider splitting the mapping domain into smaller registration graphs.

data.name: NCMAP_F63_Description
data.value: The DFS cycle detector visits each registered pair reachable from a start point; dense registration graphs can exceed the defensive visit budget (the same budget discipline as the deep-copy graph classifier). When the budget is exhausted the start point is reported as undetermined instead of crashing or blocking generation.

data.name: NCMAP041_Title
data.value: [MapWhen] predicate method resolution failed

data.name: NCMAP041_Message
data.value: [MapWhen] on property '{0}' of {1} failed to resolve predicate '{2}': {3}. The method must be declared on the annotated property's containing type (including partial parts) as public/internal static bool M(T) where the parameter equals the source field type (T1) or the source entity type (T2).

data.name: NCMAP041_Description
data.value: The attribute form of the conditional guard resolves the predicate by name on the annotated property's declaring type. Rejections cover: method not found, ambiguous overloads, non-static method, insufficient visibility (private/protected), signature mismatch (single parameter returning bool, no ref/out/in), and parameter type matching neither the source field type nor the source entity type.

data.name: NCMAP042_Title
data.value: DTO naming pattern without [MapFrom]; runtime reflection fallback unavailable under AOT

data.name: NCMAP042_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' follows the DTO naming pattern but is not annotated with [MapFrom]; source-generated mapping code cannot be produced and the runtime reflection fallback is unavailable in AOT/trimmed scenarios

data.name: NCMAP042_Description
data.value: The type name ends with Dto/DTO, which suggests it participates in object mapping. Without [MapFrom] no source-generated mapping code is produced; the runtime reflection fallback is unavailable in AOT/trimmed scenarios. Annotate [MapFrom] to enable the AOT-safe path. Types carrying mapping configuration attributes are reported as NCMAP019 (Error) instead.

data.name: NCMAP043_Title
data.value: [MapFormat] target property type must be string

data.name: NCMAP043_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with [MapFormat], but the target property type is {1}; it must be string — change the property to string or use [Convert] instead

data.name: NCMAP043_Description
data.value: [MapFormat] outputs formatted text (IFormattable.ToString(format, null)), so the target property must be string-typed.

data.name: NCMAP044_Title
data.value: [MapFormat] source property type must implement IFormattable

data.name: NCMAP044_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' is annotated with [MapFormat], but the source type {1} does not implement IFormattable — supported: DateTime/DateTimeOffset/TimeSpan/Guid/numeric/enum (including Nullable wrappers); string sources are not supported, use [Convert] instead

data.name: NCMAP044_Description
data.value: [MapFormat] binds IFormattable.ToString(string, IFormatProvider); the source property must implement IFormattable (enums qualify — Enum implements IFormattable).

data.name: NCMAP045_Title
data.value: [MapFormat] and [Convert] cannot be applied to the same property

data.name: NCMAP045_Message
data.value: [MapFormat] and [Convert] cannot both be annotated on property '{0}' — their semantics overlap; choose one of them

data.name: NCMAP045_Description
data.value: [MapFormat] (format-string output) and [Convert] (custom converter) are mutually exclusive value transforms on the same property.

data.name: NCMAP046_Title
data.value: [MapFormat] property is skipped in reverse mapping

data.name: NCMAP046_Message
data.value: Format output cannot be reverse-parsed, so property '{0}' is skipped in reverse mapping (the entity property keeps its default value). Add [ConvertBack] if the property needs round-tripping.

data.name: NCMAP046_Description
data.value: Format output is a one-way display transform (lossy and culture-dependent). Reverse mapping skips the property instead of guessing a value; declare [ConvertBack] yourself when round-tripping is needed. On the attribute side the write-back target is determined by the forward source field, so mismatched names require no extra specification.

data.name: NCMAP047_Title
data.value: Property has a mapping transform attribute but no [MapProperty] under [MapNoAutoMatch] whitelist; it is not mapped

data.name: NCMAP047_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' carries a mapping transform attribute but no [MapProperty]; under the [MapNoAutoMatch] whitelist it does not participate in mapping (not mapped, not added to candidates). Action: add an explicit [MapProperty] declaration to map it, or remove the transform attribute.

data.name: NCMAP047_Description
data.value: [MapNoAutoMatch] turns the (S,T) pair into a whitelist: only properties explicitly declared with [MapProperty] are mapped. A transform attribute ([Convert]/[Mask]/[MapFormat]/[MapWhen]) without that head declaration has no activation path (mirrors the Fluent rule that transform terminals require a Member declaration) and would otherwise be silently inert, so compilation fails fast (Error).

data.name: NCMAP_F64_Title
data.value: Fluent .Format target property type must be string

data.name: NCMAP_F64_Message
data.value: The target property '{0}' declared by .Format has type {1}; it must be string — change the property to string or use .Convert instead

data.name: NCMAP_F64_Description
data.value: .Format outputs formatted text (IFormattable.ToString(format, null)), so the target property must be string-typed.

data.name: NCMAP_F65_Title
data.value: Fluent .Format source property is unreachable or does not implement IFormattable

data.name: NCMAP_F65_Message
data.value: The source property bound by .Format for target '{0}' is {1}, which does not implement IFormattable — supported: DateTime/DateTimeOffset/TimeSpan/Guid/numeric/enum (including Nullable wrappers); use .Convert instead

data.name: NCMAP_F65_Description
data.value: .Format binds IFormattable.ToString(string, IFormatProvider); the source property must implement IFormattable (enums qualify — Enum implements IFormattable).

data.name: NCMAP_F66_Title
data.value: .Format and .Convert cannot target the same property

data.name: NCMAP_F66_Message
data.value: .Format and .Convert cannot both target property '{0}' — their semantics overlap; choose one of them

data.name: NCMAP_F66_Description
data.value: .Format (format-string output) and .Convert (custom converter) are mutually exclusive value transforms on the same anchor.

data.name: NCMAP_F67_Title
data.value: Fluent .Format property is skipped in reverse mapping

data.name: NCMAP_F67_Message
data.value: Format output cannot be reverse-parsed, so property '{0}' is skipped in reverse mapping (the entity property keeps its default value). If the property needs round-tripping, declare an explicit reverse target: .ConvertBack(converter) when the entity property has the same name, or the lambda form .ConvertBack<TEntityProp>((dto) => ...) when it has a different one (the write-back target is then read from the lambda body instead of by name).

data.name: NCMAP_F67_Description
data.value: Format output is a one-way display transform (lossy and culture-dependent). Reverse mapping skips the property instead of guessing a value; declare an explicit reverse target yourself when round-tripping is needed. A same-named entity property takes .ConvertBack(converter); a differently-named one takes the lambda form .ConvertBack<TEntityProp>((dto) => ...), which reads the write-back target (a member access on the lambda parameter) from the lambda body instead of looking it up by name.

data.name: NCMAP_F68_Title
data.value: Member declaration has no follow-up

data.name: NCMAP_F68_Message
data.value: The member '{0}' carries no declaration after Member. Add a source (From / FromSource), an ignore (Ignore), or a transform such as Mask or Format.

data.name: NCMAP_F68_Description
data.value: A bare .Member(d => d.X) with nothing following it in the member segment produces no mapping or ignore effect. The segment boundary is the next Member call, a type-pair-level terminal, or the end of the chain; at least one head declaration or config call inside the segment keeps the diagnostic silent.

data.name: NCMAP_F69_Title
data.value: Omitted source has no same-named source member

data.name: NCMAP_F69_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' has no source specified, and source type '{1}' has no member with the same name. Specify a source with .From(...).

data.name: NCMAP_F69_Description
data.value: Member-segment transforms (Mask / Format / FromJson / MapTree) resolve the source by the destination member name when From is omitted; when the source type (or FromSource sub-source) has no same-named member, the declaration would silently vanish under the legacy auto-match rule. The new form makes this an explicit error so the declaration is never lost quietly.

data.name: NCMAP_F70_Title
data.value: Same-dimension declaration repeated

data.name: NCMAP_F70_Message
data.value: Property '{0}' repeats its {1} declaration. The same slot allows only one declaration (first '{2}', duplicate '{3}').

data.name: NCMAP_F70_Description
data.value: The source slot and transform slots of a member accept a single declaration each; compile-time structure already guarantees uniqueness within one segment, so the reachable repetition is across segments (e.g. MemberHead and MemberConfig carrying the same method). Cross-segment same-slot and same-kind repetitions are rejected; the NoAutoInclude list stays idempotent (HashSet) and is out of scope.

data.name: NCMAP_F71_Title
data.value: MapWhen whole-source type argument does not match

data.name: NCMAP_F71_Message
data.value: The MapWhen type argument '{1}' on property '{0}' matches neither the target property type nor the source type '{2}'. For the whole-source form use .MapWhen<{2}>(...); for the field-value form (condition parameter of the target property type) omit the type argument.

data.name: NCMAP_F71_Description
data.value: The member-level MapWhen mixed overload pair resolves as: non-generic T1 (field-value form, inline lambda binds directly) and generic T2 (whole-source form with an explicit type argument). The explicit type argument must be the target property type or the source type; anything else is rejected so a mistyped condition never gets silently dropped.
